A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLD research by Feng and Yang. Their main text, equations, seven tables, two figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLSA and RLNN experiments on MIS, maximum clique, and maximum cut, including regularization ablations and longer-run comparisons in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–3, Figures 1–2, and Appendix B, and provides more specific training-time outcomes.

M1.justification: v2 adds an optional epsilon offset to RLSA's flipping threshold in Equation 14 and Algorithm 1. Appendix A.3 replaces the documented node-selection decoder with iterative flips of the coordinate having the largest energy decrease. The main sampling framework, RLNN loss, and GCN architecture remain.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MIS on RB and ER graphs, maximum clique on RB graphs, and maximum cut on BA graphs at the same scales, including transfer testing on large ER graphs. Categorical variables and traveling-salesman problems are discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: The solution-quality and inference-time comparisons retain the same methods; ERDOES is renamed EGN with identical scores. v2 additionally introduces an explicit training-time comparison against DiffUCO in Section 5.2 and Appendix A.2, using its cited two-day training time.

E3.justification: The stated validation-set size changes from 500 graphs in v1 Section 4.1 to 100 in v2 Section 5.1. Appendix A.3 also changes the postprocessing procedure. Training/test counts, evaluation metrics, and tabulated hyperparameters remain unchanged; these reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 drops v1 Section 4.2's brief comparison at equal sampling-step and trial counts, which reported that RLNN could sometimes outperform RLSA. The displayed LD step-size ablation, RLNN regularization ablation, training curves, and Appendix B's tenfold-step comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean primal-gap curves with standard-deviation shading in Figure 1. Sampling-trial counts remain unchanged, and no new seed information, repeated-evaluation practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and both figure images are unchanged. v2 newly specifies training under half an hour for small graphs except ER on eight A6000 GPUs, where v1 gave an overall under-one-hour bound, and adds the cited DiffUCO training-time comparison. It removes the qualitative equal-step/trial RLNN advantage reported in v1; these are reporting changes, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the inconsistent L2-distance constraint with Hamming distance and corrects the locally balanced proposal to a probability-ratio/kernel formulation, noting that regularization can break kernel symmetry. It also specializes MIS/clique formulas to unit weights and corrects the clique objective sign and missing gradients in the normalized-gradient analogy. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about RLD, local-optimum escape, and RLSA's speed-quality advantage remain. v2 sharpens the RLNN contribution into an explicit training-efficiency advantage over previous diffusion models, including in the introduction and conclusion, beyond v1's more general local-objective efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 interprets RLNN's lower performance relative to RLSA through approximate gradients and less prior knowledge, replacing discussion of balancing per-step computation against search effort. It adds the possible loss of local balance under regularization and makes applicability boundaries more specific by naming categorical variables and globally constrained problems such as TSP.

D1.justification: v2 adds the authors' code-access URL, an explicit iSCO source-code link, and float32 training precision. It gives finer training-time details and explains the average-versus-total runtime discrepancy motivating the iSCO rerun. Hardware, float16 inference, optimizer settings, and Appendix C's example code were already present.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially expands its positioning: v2 distinguishes GWG's local neighborhood, PAS/PAFS's sequential sampling, and discrete LD's parallel proposals, then positions RLD around their respective limitations. It also develops the contrast with diffusion training and adds several works, including Cappart et al., Feng and colleagues, and Yau et al., while removing some earlier references.

P1.justification: Broad paragraph rewrites span the introduction, method explanations, experimental discussion, and appendices. Related Work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, its subsections are reordered and expanded, and terminology, grammatical errors, and appendix headings are revised.

P2.justification: The two figure images and seven table structures are retained. v2 expands Figure 1's caption, corrects Table 2's excluded-solver caption from KaMIS to SDP, updates ERDOES/EGN and RLNN category labels, and reflows displays around the reorganized text without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency, explains its relationship to prior methods more clearly, and adds useful code-access and precision information. These are supported gains in clarity and reproducibility. The empirical tables and figures remain unchanged, while the revised validation and postprocessing descriptions are not explicitly reconciled with those outputs, limiting the overall improvement.
